item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
They've only tried to open it 62 times? That doesn't seem like enough of a sample size for actuarial tables to come into play. Unless the intent is that the anomaly uses the most likely scenario that would prevent opening?
Also, that's not nearly enough attempts for good scientific rigor.

This calls for experimentation!
Construct a scenario with as close to zero chance of anything going wrong as possible. Declare war on Murphy's Law.
Start with putting your designated opener through every medical test there is; proceed only once they are certified as the healthiest human being ever documented. Keep them under constant quarantine and heavy guard. Transport to the tectonically stable testing site via armored car; etc., etc.
When circumstances conspire to prevent the opening anyway; add steps to prevent that particular chain of events and repeat from square one.
After several hundred failed attempts, and an accumulated protocol that looks like a genre-savvy protagonist in a Final Destination movie; only then would it be fitting for the Foundation powers that be to declare an end to the attempts as a waste of resources.

That might make for an entertaining collaborative tale/test log. Each new contributor starts by explaining how the last entry was foiled, before writing up their own attempt to circumvent all earlier failure states.
